name: str_replace
title: Replace the first match with new text

origin.description: Replaces the first match of a pattern in each string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A regular expression by default. fixed() compares literal text and coll() uses collation. A boundary, including the empty string, is an error when replacement is text.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: Usually one string, or a vector the same length as string or pattern. \1, \2, and so on insert capture groups. A function receives the matched pieces and returns text of any length. NA_character_ makes a matched string missing.

origin.details: The first match in each string is replaced. string, pattern, and replacement are recycled together. A function is given the matched substrings; on that path an empty pattern matches characters, and a missing return leaves the original string unchanged.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as string, pattern, or replacement.
origin.example:
fruits <- c("one apple", "two pears", "three bananas")
writeLines(c(
  str_replace(fruits, "[aeiou]", "-"),
  str_replace(fruits, "([aeiou])", "\\1\\1"),
  str_replace(fruits, "[aeiou]", c("1", "2", "3")),
  str_replace(fruits, c("a", "e", "i"), "-")
))

translation.description: Replaces the first match of a pattern in each string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings and stringi._na.NA. NULL is an empty list.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A string or list is an ICU regular expression. fixed, coll, and regex come from stringr.pattern. A boundary, including "", is an error when replacement is text.

arguments.name: replacement
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings. \\1 is capture group 1. A callable receives the matched pieces as one list. NA makes a matched string missing.

translation.details: Text replacement calls stringi's first-replace functions. A callable is located with stringi and written back with stri_sub_replace, omit_na true, so a missing return leaves that string unchanged. An empty pattern on the callable path is a character boundary.
translation.value: A list of strings. Names on the input are kept when pattern has length 1 or the same length as string.
translation.example:
from stringr.pattern import fixed
from stringr.replace import str_replace
fruits = ["one apple", "two pears", "three bananas"]
rows = []
rows.extend(str_replace(fruits, "[aeiou]", "-"))
rows.extend(str_replace(fruits, "([aeiou])", "\\1\\1"))
rows.extend(str_replace(fruits, "[aeiou]", ["1", "2", "3"]))
rows.extend(str_replace(fruits, ["a", "e", "i"], "-"))
for item in rows:
    print(item)
